theorems.theorem_title: Proposition 6.19 — one classical sampler from linear defect
theorems.preamble:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_QuantumKtSoI_qKt
import Definitions.Def_QuantumKtSoI_PolySampler
import Definitions.Def_QuantumKtSoI_PSPACEHard

open Classical
theorems.formal_statement:
namespace QuantumKtSoI

/-- **Proposition 6.19** (One classical sampler from linear defect; Myrisiotis, STOC 2027
submission, held version sha256 6616571c…, p.91). There is one classical polynomial-time sampler
`S`, outputting two `n`-bit strings on input `1ⁿ`, with the following property. If some `η > 0`
satisfies `Δ(u,v) > η(|u|+|v|)` for infinitely many pairs, then, for every real `C ≥ 1`, there is
an integer `d_C ≥ 1` such that `Pr_{(X,Y)∼S(1ⁿ)}[Δ(X,Y) > C log(2n+2)] ≥ n^{−d_C}` for infinitely
many `n`. The sampler is independent of `η` and `C`, and its running time is polynomial on every
branch.

**Formalization Note** The sampler is a `PolySampler` (a §2.1 probabilistic Turing machine with an
all-branch polynomial deadline and `2n`-bit outputs `XY = ⟨X,Y⟩`), chosen before `η` and `C`.
"Infinitely many `n`" is `∀ N, ∃ n ≥ N`; `n^{−d}` is `1/nᵈ`. Logarithms are base 2. -/
theorem proposition_6_19 (G : GlueRoutines) (hG : G.Admissible) :
    ∃ S : PolySampler,
      (∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧
        {p : List Bool × List Bool |
          η * ((p.1.length + p.2.length : ℕ) : ℝ) < (defect G p.1 p.2 : ℝ)}.Infinite) →
      ∀ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N,
        1 / (n : ℝ) ^ d ≤
          S.prob n fun X Y => C * Real.logb 2 (2 * n + 2) < (defect G X Y : ℝ) := by sorry

end QuantumKtSoI

theorems.theorem_title: Theorem 6.20 with Theorem 6.21 — one classical sampler exceeds a symmetry defect of $C\log(2n+2)$ for every $C\ge1$
theorems.preamble:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_QuantumKtSoI_qKt
import Definitions.Def_QuantumKtSoI_PolySampler
import Definitions.Def_QuantumKtSoI_PSPACEHard

open Classical
theorems.formal_statement:
namespace QuantumKtSoI

/-- **Theorem 6.20** (Classical sampling of symmetry violations; native case of Theorem 1.1;
Myrisiotis, *Failure of Symmetry of Information for Quantum Computations*, STOC 2027 submission,
held version sha256 6616571c…, p.92), together with **Theorem 6.21** (The same classical sampler
under logarithmic comparison, p.95).

There is one classical polynomial-time sampler `S`, outputting two `n`-bit strings on every input
`1ⁿ`, such that, for every real `C ≥ 1`, there is an integer `d_C ≥ 1` with
`Pr_{(X,Y)∼S(1ⁿ)}[Δ(X,Y) > C log(2n+2)] > n^{−d_C}` for infinitely many `n`. The sampler is
independent of `C`, and its running time is polynomial on every branch. (Theorem 6.21) For every
conditional cost function `µ` with `|µ(v|u) − qKt(v|u)| ≤ B_µ log(|u|+|v|+2) + B_µ` for all `u, v`
and some `B_µ ≥ 0`, and every real `C ≥ 1`, there is an integer `d_{µ,C} ≥ 1` with
`Pr_{(X,Y)∼S(1ⁿ)}[Δ_µ(X,Y) > C log(2n+2)] > n^{−d_{µ,C}}` for infinitely many `n`, for the same `S`.

**Formalization Note** The paper's glue routines are fixed only by their properties (p.24); the
statement asserts that admissible routine sets exist and that the conclusion holds for every one
of them, with `S` chosen after the routine set and before `C` and `µ`. The sampler is a
`PolySampler` (a §2.1 probabilistic Turing machine with an all-branch deadline `c(n+2)^k` whose
`2n`-bit output `XY` is the pair `⟨X,Y⟩`). "Infinitely many `n`" is `∀ N, ∃ n ≥ N`; `n^{−d}` is
`1/nᵈ`; `µ` is real-valued (the comparison hypothesis forces finite values);
`Δ_µ(x,y) = µ(x) + µ(y|x) − µ(⟨x,y⟩)` with `µ(v) = µ(v|ε)`, and `µ v u` stands for `µ(v|u)`.
Logarithms are base 2. -/
theorem theorem_6_20 :
    (∃ G : GlueRoutines, G.Admissible) ∧
      ∀ G : GlueRoutines, G.Admissible →
        ∃ S : PolySampler,
          (∀ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N,
            1 / (n : ℝ) ^ d <
              S.prob n fun X Y => C * Real.logb 2 (2 * n + 2) < (defect G X Y : ℝ)) ∧
          ∀ μ : List Bool → List Bool → ℝ,
            (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ u v : List Bool,
              |μ v u - qKt G v u| ≤ B * Real.logb 2 (u.length + v.length + 2) + B) →
            ∀ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N,
              1 / (n : ℝ) ^ d <
                S.prob n fun X Y => C * Real.logb 2 (2 * n + 2) < μ X [] + μ Y X - μ (pair X Y) [] := by sorry

end QuantumKtSoI

import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_QuantumKtSoI_qKt

open Classical
theorems.formal_statement:
namespace QuantumKtSoI

/-- **Lemma 5.12** (Padded pairs; Myrisiotis, STOC 2027 submission, held version sha256 6616571c…,
p.60). There is a constant `c_q` such that, for all strings `u, v` and every integer
`λ > max(|u|,|v|)`, with `û = pad_λ(u)` and `v̂ = pad_λ(v)`,
`qKt(v|u) − qKt(⟨u,v⟩) + qKt(u) ≤ qKt(v̂|û) − qKt(⟨û,v̂⟩) + qKt(û) + c_q log(λ+2)`. -/
theorem lemma_5_12 (G : GlueRoutines) (hG : G.Admissible) :
    ∃ cq : ℝ, ∀ (u v : List Bool) (lam : ℕ), max u.length v.length < lam →
      (qKt G v u : ℝ) - qKt G (pair u v) [] + qKt G u [] ≤
        (qKt G (pad lam v) (pad lam u) : ℝ) - qKt G (pair (pad lam u) (pad lam v)) [] +
          qKt G (pad lam u) [] + cq * Real.logb 2 (lam + 2) := by sorry

end QuantumKtSoI

theorems.theorem_title: Theorem 2.7 — DQI+USD efficiently Gibbs-samples $\mathbb G_{\mathrm{ER}}(N,k,D)$ at every $\beta<\tanh^{-1}(K_*(k)/D)$
theorems.preamble:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_IsingLTL_BeliefProp_TVDist
import Definitions.Def_DQIShattered_DQI
import Definitions.Def_DQIShattered_Efficient
theorems.formal_statement:
namespace DQIShattered

open Filter Topology

/-- Zhou, Shutty, Sellke, Jordan, *Gibbs Sampling in the Shattered Phase by Decoded Quantum Interferometry*,
arXiv:2609.40345, held version sha256 0c7f6fdf…, Theorem 2.7 (Gibbs sampling by DQI+USD), p.7.

Fix `k ≥ 3`, `D ≥ k` and `δ ∈ (0, 1)`; let `(B, J) ∼ 𝔾_ER(N, k, D)`.

**(A) Decoding.** For every `γ ∈ [0, γ_USD(k, D))` there is a polynomial-time decoder family solving the
`(B, γ, δ)`-quantum decoding problem with probability `1 − o_N(1)` over `B`.

**(B) Sampling.** For every `ε > 0` and every `β ≥ 0` with `β < β_ALG(k, D) = tanh⁻¹(K_*(k)/D)`, and
`γ = 1/2 − (1/2) sech β`:

1. *(DQI)* there is a decoder family as in (A) at this `γ` (its machine reading the digits of `β`) such that the exact DQI output law `ν^{DQI}_{B,J,β}`
   built from its decoder unitaries is within total variation `ε` of `µ_{β,H_{B,J}}` with probability at least
   `1 − √δ/ε − o_N(1)` over `(B, J)`, for every fixed `z₀`;
2. *(efficiently, by DQI)* there is a polynomial-time sampler family over `{H, T, CNOT}` that implements this DQI
   sampler: on every instance its output law is within total variation `η_N → 0` of `ν^{DQI}_{B,J,β}` (built from
   the same decoder circuits, with `z₀ = (+1, …, +1)`), and it is within total variation `ε` of `µ_{β,H_{B,J}}` with
   probability at least `1 − √δ/ε − o_N(1)` over `(B, J)`.

**Formalization Note** "Efficiently" is a Turing machine writing a circuit over `{H, T, CNOT}` of polynomial size in
polynomial time (`EfficientDecoders`, `EfficientSamplers`), on input the instance and the first `N` binary places
of the real parameter (`γ` in (A); `β` in (B), for the decoders as well as the sampler, so that the sampler's machine
can write the decoder circuits it runs). Every existential (machine, constants, `o`) comes after `k, D, δ` and the clause's own
parameters, and before `N`; `o_N(1)` absorbs "sufficiently large `N`". `β < tanh⁻¹(K_*(k)/D)` with `β ≥ 0` is
`tanh β < K_*(k)/D`. -/
theorem theorem_2_7 (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (D : ℝ) (hD : (k : ℝ) ≤ D) (δ : ℝ) (hδ0 : 0 < δ)
    (hδ1 : δ < 1) :
    (∀ γ : ℝ, 0 ≤ γ → γ < gammaUSD k D → ∃ circ, EfficientDecoders k D γ δ (fun N => encReal N γ) circ) ∧
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ β : ℝ, 0 ≤ β → Real.tanh β < Kstar k / D →
      ∃ circ, EfficientDecoders k D (gammaOf β) δ (fun N => encReal N β) circ ∧
        (∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, k ≤ N → ∀ x₀ : Fin N → ZMod 2,
          1 - Real.sqrt δ / ε - o N ≤ erProb N k D fun B v =>
            IsingLTL.BeliefProp.tvDist
              (nuDQI B v β (decoderMatrix (Mrows N k D) (circ N B))
                (zeroWork ((circ N B).wires - 2 * Mrows N k D)) x₀) (gibbs B v β) ≤ ε) ∧
        ∃ circ', EfficientSamplers k D β circ' ∧
          (∃ η : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto η atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, k ≤ N →
            ∀ E : Fin (Mrows N k D) → KSet N k, ∀ v : Fin (Mrows N k D) → ZMod 2,
              IsingLTL.BeliefProp.tvDist (samplerDist N (circ' N (incidence E) v))
                (nuDQI (incidence E) v β (decoderMatrix (Mrows N k D) (circ N (incidence E)))
                  (zeroWork ((circ N (incidence E)).wires - 2 * Mrows N k D)) 0) ≤ η N) ∧
          ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, k ≤ N →
            1 - Real.sqrt δ / ε - o N ≤ erProb N k D fun B v =>
              IsingLTL.BeliefProp.tvDist (samplerDist N (circ' N B v)) (gibbs B v β) ≤ ε := by sorry

end DQIShattered

theorems.theorem_title: Theorem 4.7 — correctness of Algorithm 3: simultaneous $\gamma$-CVP for all but a $2^{-\Omega(n^{2/3})}$ fraction of $H$
theorems.preamble:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_QaryCVP_qaryLattice
import Definitions.Def_QaryCVP_matAvg
import Definitions.Def_QaryCVP_ent3
import Definitions.Def_QaryCVP_corrAttempt
import Definitions.Def_QaryCVP_alg3

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
theorems.formal_statement:
namespace QaryCVP

/-- **Theorem 4.7** (correctness of Algorithm 3). Kim, Kwon, Lee, Lee, STOC 2027 submission
manuscript (sha256 9aeb2ff4…ab4), Theorem 4.7, p.39; Algorithm 3, p.33; (11), p.33; (15), p.34;
Lemma 4.1 and Lemma 4.2, p.35; Definition 3.4, p.24.

Fix a constant `p ∈ (0, 3/4]` and bounds of a compact parameter set:
`0 < β₋ ≤ β ≤ β₊ < 1`, `c ≥ β + κ`, `c ≤ c₊`, and the margin `κ > 0` of (11). There is a rational
`C > 0`, depending only on these, such that for every rational `γ > 1` the following holds. Run
Algorithm 3 (the model `alg3`) with parameters `β, c` chosen from `n, m, q` alone in that compact set,
with (11) with margin `κ` on the binary correction branch (`β ≤ 1/4 − κ`, `h(β) ≥ 3/4 + κ`), with
exact procedures `A` (Lemma 4.1: a closest point of `Λ`) and `E_{γ^{−2}}` (Definition 3.4), with `S`
for `q ≥ 3` and `S₂` for `q = 2`, and `r = ⌈Cn⌉` attempts, where

* whenever the algorithm reaches the correction branch with `q ≥ 3` in sufficiently large
  dimension, `S` returns `⊥` or `v ∈ {−1, 0, 1}^{n₀}` with `Av = t`, `‖v‖² ≤ βn₀`, and all but a
  `2^{−Ω(n₀^{2/3})}` fraction of matrices `A` have success probability at least `p`, averaged over
  uniform `t` and its randomness (uniformly over the chosen parameters, at the actual rate);
* `S₂` is a binary sampler with the guarantees of Lemma 4.2 (output `⊥` or a `0/1` vector of weight
  at most `⌊βn₀⌋` solving `Av = t`; average success `≥ 105/128` except for a fraction (18)).

Then for all sufficiently large `n` and all integers `q ≥ 2`, `m ≥ 0` with `δ ≤ 3/2`, for all but a
`2^{−Ω(n^{2/3})}` fraction of `H`, with `H` fixed,
`Pr_ω[for every y ∈ Qⁿ the algorithm returns x ∈ Λ with ‖x − y‖ ≤ γ min_{a∈Λ}‖a − y‖] ≥ 1 − 2^{−Ω(n)}`,
`ω` being the attempts' random bits, shared by all targets.

**Formalization Note.** Decision 4: the subprocedures are arbitrary functions meeting their
specifications (a generalization: any implementation). The compact subset of
`{(β, c) : 0 < β < 1, c > β}` is written as the box `β₋ ≤ β ≤ β₊`, `β + κ ≤ c ≤ c₊`; every compact
subset lies in such a box and every such box is compact. The solvers' randomness is one probability
space `(Ω, μ)` with measurable outcome events. `2^{−Ω(·)}` is `∃ c > 0, N` (R4); fractions are counts
over the `q^{mn}` matrices (R5). `C` is chosen before `γ` and the procedures. -/
theorem theorem_4_7 (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p ≤ 3 / 4) (βlo βhi chi κ : ℝ)
    (hβlo : 0 < βlo) (hβ : βlo ≤ βhi) (hβhi : βhi < 1) (hκ : 0 < κ) :
    ∃ C : ℚ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ γ : ℚ, 1 < γ →
    ∀ {Ω : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
      (β c : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℚ) (feas : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop)
      (Aex : ∀ {m n q : ℕ}, Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) (ZMod q) → (Fin n → ℚ) → (Fin n → ℤ))
      (Eex : ∀ {m n q : ℕ}, Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) (ZMod q) → (Fin n → ℚ) → ℚ →
        Option (Fin n → ℤ))
      (S S₂ : ℕ → ∀ {m n0 q : ℕ}, Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n0) (ZMod q) → (Fin m → ZMod q) → Ω →
        Option (Fin n0 → ℤ)),
      (∀ n m q : ℕ, βlo ≤ β n m q ∧ β n m q ≤ βhi ∧ (β n m q : ℝ) + κ ≤ c n m q ∧
        (c n m q : ℝ) ≤ chi) →
      (∀ n m : ℕ, ReachesCorr β feas n m 2 →
        (β n m 2 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 4 - κ ∧ 3 / 4 + κ ≤ binEnt (β n m 2)) →
      (∀ (m n q : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) (ZMod q)) (y : Fin n → ℚ), 1 ≤ m → 1 ≤ n →
        2 ≤ q → IsClosest H y (Aex H y)) →
      (∀ (m n q : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) (ZMod q)) (y : Fin n → ℚ) (b : ℚ), 1 ≤ n →
        2 ≤ q → 0 ≤ b → IsSearchOutput (fun _ => True) H y b (Eex H y b)) →
      (∀ (n m n0 q : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n0) (ZMod q)) (t : Fin m → ZMod q)
        (o : Option (Fin n0 → ℤ)),
        MeasurableSet {ω | S n A t ω = o} ∧ MeasurableSet {ω | S₂ n A t ω = o}) →
      (∃ c₀ : ℝ, 0 < c₀ ∧ ∃ N₀ : ℕ,
        (∀ n m q : ℕ, N₀ ≤ n → 3 ≤ q → DensityLeThreeHalves q m n → ReachesCorr β feas n m q →
          (∀ (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin (n0A β n m q).toNat) (ZMod q)) (t : Fin m → ZMod q) ω v,
            S n A t ω = some v → (∀ i, v i = -1 ∨ v i = 0 ∨ v i = 1) ∧
              A.mulVec (fun j => (v j : ZMod q)) = t ∧
              sqNormZ v ≤ β n m q * (n0A β n m q).toNat) ∧
          1 - (2 : ℝ) ^ (-c₀ * ((n0A β n m q).toNat : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)) ≤
            matFrac q m (n0A β n m q).toNat (fun A =>
              p ≤ vecAvg q m (fun t => (μ {ω | (S n A t ω).isSome}).toReal))) ∧
        (∀ n m : ℕ, N₀ ≤ n → DensityLeThreeHalves 2 m n → ReachesCorr β feas n m 2 →
          (∀ (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin (n0A β n m 2).toNat) (ZMod 2)) (t : Fin m → ZMod 2) ω v,
            S₂ n A t ω = some v → (∀ i, v i = 0 ∨ v i = 1) ∧
              (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => v i = 1)).card ≤
                ⌊β n m 2 * (n0A β n m 2).toNat⌋₊ ∧
              A.mulVec (fun j => (v j : ZMod 2)) = t) ∧
          1 - ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((m : ℤ) - (n0A β n m 2).toNat) +
              32 * (2 : ℝ) ^ m / (ballCard (n0A β n m 2).toNat (β n m 2) : ℝ)) ≤
            matFrac 2 m (n0A β n m 2).toNat (fun A =>
              (105 / 128 : ℝ) ≤ vecAvg 2 m (fun t => (μ {ω | (S₂ n A t ω).isSome}).toReal)))) →
      ∃ c₁ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ ∃ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₂ ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n m q : ℕ, N ≤ n → 2 ≤ q →
        DensityLeThreeHalves q m n →
        1 - (2 : ℝ) ^ (-c₁ * (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)) ≤
          matFrac q m n (fun H =>
            let E : Set (Alg3Coins C β n m q Ω) :=
              {ω | ∀ y : Fin n → ℚ, IsApproxCVP γ H y (alg3 γ C β c feas Aex Eex S S₂ H y ω)}
            MeasurableSet E ∧ 1 - (2 : ℝ) ^ (-c₂ * n) ≤ (alg3Measure C β n m q μ E).toReal) := by sorry

end QaryCVP

theorems.theorem_title: Lemma 9.2 — one program implements Algorithms 1 and 2 in $O(\log n\log\log n)$ bits
theorems.preamble:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_Strings
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_Pad
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_ParseTree
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_Build
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_LinearMaps
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_HashFamily
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_Counters
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_SeededHash
import Definitions.Def_DynBrooks_Machine
import Definitions.Def_ExactPatternStream_StreamRun

open MeasureTheory
theorems.formal_statement:
namespace ExactPatternStream

/-- Gawrychowski, Janczewski, Jin, Nelson, *An Improved Streaming Algorithm for Exact Pattern Matching* (preprint, STOC 2027 submission, sha256 351218cb…), Lemma 9.2, p.29 (PDF 30), with the procedure of §9.

For `m ≤ n ≤ 2m`, one program implements the matching answers of Algorithms 1 and 2 in one pass, reports each answer before the next character is read, and uses `O(log n log log n)` bits. Its seeds come from its coin tape: there is a measurable map `Φ` from tapes to `(ω, a_R)` whose law is the uniform one, and a run's answers are those of `Match(P, T)` at `Φ` of its tape.

**Formalization Note.** The machine is `DynBrooks.Program`, as in the goal, with word size `cw · ℓ(n)`; `|Σ| ≤ n^{O(1)}` is `∀ k`; `Q, cw, K, p_R` come before the input (the program chooses `p_R`, with `log p_R = O(log m)`, p.22). Space is for **every** tape at **every** step. A tape on which rejection sampling never ends has no completed state; these form a null set. The last clause, on partial runs, says the answers so far agree with `Match` at some seeds, for **every** tape: this is what makes the error one-sided on every tape, as `Match`'s completeness holds at all seeds. -/
theorem lemma_9_2 : ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ (Q : DynBrooks.Program) (cw K : ℕ) (pR : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Nat.Primes),
    ∀ (σ : ℕ) (P T : List (Fin σ)),
    1 ≤ P.length → P.length ≤ T.length → T.length ≤ 2 * P.length → 3 ≤ T.length →
    σ ≤ T.length ^ k →
    let m := P.length
    let n := T.length
    let w := cw * ell n
    let B : ℝ := (K : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 n * Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 n)
    let p : ℕ := pR n m σ
    2 ^ (4 * bigL σ m) < p ∧ Real.logb 2 p ≤ (K : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 n ∧
    (∀ (ω : ℕ → BitVec w) (t : ℕ),
      (spaceBits w (DynBrooks.run Q ω (startConfig w P T) t) : ℝ) ≤ B) ∧
    (∀ (ω : ℕ → BitVec w) (j : ℕ) (c : DynBrooks.Config w), j < m + n →
      streamState Q P T ω j = some c → ∀ t : ℕ,
        (spaceBits w (DynBrooks.run Q ω (DynBrooks.feed c [(streamWords P T).getD j 0]) t) : ℝ) ≤ B) ∧
    (∀ (ω : ℕ → BitVec w) (j : ℕ) (c : DynBrooks.Config w), j ≤ m + n →
      streamState Q P T ω j = some c → c.output.length = (j + 1) - 2 * m) ∧
    ProbAtLeast (DynBrooks.coinMeasure w)
      {ω | ∀ j ≤ m + n, (streamState Q P T ω j).isSome} 1 ∧
    ∃ Φ : (ℕ → BitVec w) → Seeds σ m × ZMod (pR n m σ : ℕ),
      (∀ E : Set (Seeds σ m × ZMod (pR n m σ : ℕ)), MeasurableSet (Φ ⁻¹' E) ∧
        DynBrooks.coinMeasure w (Φ ⁻¹' E) =
          ENNReal.ofReal (unifProb fun s => s ∈ E)) ∧
      (∀ (ω : ℕ → BitVec w) (c : DynBrooks.Config w), streamState Q P T ω (m + n) = some c →
        c.output = answersOf P T (seededMatch P T (Φ ω))) ∧
      ∀ (ω : ℕ → BitVec w) (j : ℕ) (c : DynBrooks.Config w), j ≤ m + n →
        streamState Q P T ω j = some c →
        ∃ s : Seeds σ m × ZMod (pR n m σ : ℕ), c.output <+: answersOf P T (seededMatch P T s) := by sorry

end ExactPatternStream

/-- The finite-experiment certificate with an explicit deterministic feasibility
algorithm. It still leaves concrete register-machine realization to a later proof. -/
theorem CountingMatroid.Bridge.finite_experiment_fpras_explicit :
    ∃ (C d : ℕ), 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (n r : ℕ) (M₁ M₂ : Matroid (Fin n))
        (O : OAI.CommonBasesFPRAS.IndependenceOracle n) (p : InputParams),
        M₁.E = Set.univ → M₂.E = Set.univ →
        M₁.eRank = (r : ℕ∞) → M₂.eRank = (r : ℕ∞) →
        OAI.CommonBasesFPRAS.ExactOracles M₁ M₂ O →
        let K := (Program.schedule n p).val.repetitions * blockLength n r p
        let B := OAI.CommonBasesFPRAS.resourceBound C d n r p.ε p.δ
        let Z := OAI.CommonBasesFPRAS.commonBaseCount M₁ M₂
        K ≤ B ∧
        (Set.ncard {bits : List Bool | bits.length = K ∧
          ((presampledOutcome Analysis.IntersectionSearch.intersectionSolver n r (O false) (O true) p bits).1 < (1-p.ε)*(Z:ℚ) ∨
          (1+p.ε)*(Z:ℚ) < (presampledOutcome Analysis.IntersectionSearch.intersectionSolver n r (O false) (O true) p bits).1)} : ENNReal)
            * (1/2 : ENNReal)^K ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (p.δ : ℝ) ∧
        ∀ bits : List Bool, bits.length = K →
          let out := presampledOutcome Analysis.IntersectionSearch.intersectionSolver n r (O false) (O true) p bits
          0 ≤ out.1 ∧ (Z = 0 → out.1 = 0) ∧
          out.2.oracleCalls ≤ B ∧ out.2.bitOps ≤ B := by
  sorry
